categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build succeeds with 0 errors; all 10 warnings are the scaffold's pre-existing ImageSharp NU1902/NU1903 advisories. / returns 200 via the '/' domain on the Blog page and lists both posts as cards with hero image, date, title and excerpt; links work. Both posts render every block (richTextBlock, quoteBlock, imageBlock; heroBlock on the front page) with no fallbacks. 4 provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs (6/6 load). All content published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: 4 element blocks in Blocks, blogFrontPage/blogPost in Pages, siteRoot untouched in Repositories. Block grid 7/7: one 'Blog Block Grid' (Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) with hero, rich text, image (with caption) and quote blocks, used on both page types; posts are split over 3-4 blocks. Structure 5/5: siteRoot only at root and allows blogFrontPage, blogFrontPage allows only blogPost, default templates assigned, camelCase aliases. Hygiene 4/5: no compositions and excerpt/heroImage are real properties, but there is no publish-date property (the listing shows UpdateDate), and blogFrontPage's 'intro' property is filled but never rendered.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml render blocks with Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); scaffold blockgrid partials unchanged. One adapter per alias in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/ (heroBlock, richTextBlock, imageBlock, quoteBlock), each taking BlockGridItem<T>, mapping to a record in Models/Blocks/ and calling Component.InvokeAsync with no markup. One ViewComponent each (Hero, RichText, Image, Quote) rendering Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml with plain-model-only views. Program.cs/appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, friendly Children<T>/Url()/GetCropUrl, Tailwind built into wwwroot/dist/site.css.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Writing 4/6: both posts are on topic and accurate (n×m→n+m integration problem, runtime capability discovery, MCP across IDEs/agents/CI; composable block-based pages built over MCP), with relevant photos and a credited caption. But they are short: post 1 has four paragraphs and a quote, and post 2 has only two paragraphs around one image. Presentation 4/4: a coherent dark Tailwind design with a header, a hero, a two-column card listing, a readable max-w-3xl article column, a styled blockquote and a footer.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema went through umbraco (dev MCP) and pages/blocks/publishing through umbraco-editor, in the prescribed order: model → content → stop/build/restart → Razor. No Management API, DB, uSync or migration use; no memory or out-of-folder access; no warnings. The final report is accurate: it lists what was built, the URLs (it ran on its own http port 41576) and pre-existing warnings, and it claims nothing false.

summary: A clean, fully working MCP-built blog: 4 reusable blocks (hero, rich text, image, quote) on a shared block grid, a front page with image/date/excerpt cards, and two posts, rendered through a textbook adapter → ViewComponent pipeline with a polished dark Tailwind design. The only weaknesses are short posts (the second has just two paragraphs) and no real publish-date property.
strengths: Every automated check passes (43/43); build, routing, domain, media and publishing all correct
Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, plain records in Models/Blocks, one ViewComponent per block
Clean schema: correct folders, a single custom block grid in /Custom, right allowed children and templates
Polished, coherent dark design with a real card listing and readable article pages
Followed the MCP channel and order of operations exactly; honest final report
